text.p: These are the main headlines reported on the Latvian State Radio on Thursday in the early afternoon. Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
- Some 800 kg of fuel oil has been gathered on the western coast since clean-up operations began after an oil spill hit the coastline.

- Parliament passed a law on pharmaceuticals law which allows medicines from EU countries to enter Latvia without prior control, which has been criticised by the welfare ministry. It says there is no unified system in place in the EU which might lead to a lack of control.

- The first 10 aliens' pasports were handed out today. Russian ambassador Udalts has voiced his criticsm against the move saying the document violates a number of international conventions. The passports are given to residents who do not have Latvian citizenship, who are mostly Russian-speakers.
